ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL — Clicking any sidebar nav link (NavLink to='dashboard', 'profile', 'catalogue', ...) causes infinite React render loop with URL segment accumulation: /martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard → /dashboard/dashboard → /dashboard/dashboard/dashboard... Chrome console throws 'Maximum update depth exceeded' repeatedly. The catch-all Route path='*' → Navigate to='dashboard' inside the nested Routes recursively re-appends segments because NavLink `to` values are relative to the current URL, not the parent portal route. Impact: user CANNOT navigate between portal pages via sidebar — they'd only be able to reach pages via direct URL / refresh / quick-action Link with `../` prefix (which QuickActions correctly use).

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix SellerPortalApp sidebar NavLink infinite navigation loop. In /app/frontend/src/apps/martbaked-sellers/SellerPortalApp.jsx line 145, NavLink `to={n.to}` (values: 'dashboard','profile',...) is relative to the CURRENT URL under a splat route, so at /martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard the resolved href becomes /martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard/dashboard. The catch-all <Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='dashboard' replace/>}/> then matches and redirects again, causing the setState loop. Fix options: (a) change NAV entries to absolute paths and build them from the resolved sellerSlug: `to={`/martbaked/${slug}/portal/${n.to}`}`; OR (b) add `relative='path'` and use `to={`../${n.to}`}`; OR (c) remove the catch-all Navigate (rely on index redirect only) and make NavLink `end` where needed. Option (a) is safest.
Consider making test rerun idempotent by handling detail shape when Echo already approved (minor).
critical_code_review_comments: SellerPortalApp.jsx L218-228 — the nested <Routes> is fine, but the combination of splat catch-all `<Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='dashboard' replace/>}/>` + relative NavLink `to='dashboard'` creates an infinite-loop trap. This is the P0 blocker.

SellerPortalApp.jsx L198-208 — legacy redirect useEffect depends on `supplier`, and when `sellerSlug !== supplier.seller_slug` it navigates unconditionally. If a rogue nav pushes an intermediate URL, this could recompute and re-navigate — verify the guard against re-firing after successful redirect (currently `sellerSlug !== supplier.seller_slug` gate handles it, OK).

shared/suppliers/routes.py L742-749 — slug regex `re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '', raw.split(' ')[0].lower())` strips hyphens BEFORE the collision suffix step, so a trading_name like 'Echo-Fresh' collapses to 'echofresh'. Consider allowing hyphens: `re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]+', '', ...)`. Also, splitting only on space misses hyphenated first words. Non-blocking, but review the slug normalisation intent.

shared/suppliers/routes.py L744 — the `while` loop for collision uses `n = 1` initial but re-checks `candidate` (which is still `base` on first iteration), so if base collides once you get 'base-2'. That matches the spec 'echo, else echo-2'. Good.

rca of the issue: SellerPortalApp.jsx sidebar NavLink infinite loop RCA — react-router v6 resolves relative NavLink `to` values against the CURRENT location by default, not against the parent Route path when the Route uses a splat (`/martbaked/:sellerSlug/portal/*`). Combined with the nested `<Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='dashboard' replace/>}/>` catch-all in SellerPortalApp, clicking a NavLink at `/martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard` builds href `/martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard/dashboard`; that URL matches the splat again, matches the inner `*` catch-all, redirects to relative `dashboard` → `/martbaked/delta/portal/dashboard/dashboard/dashboard`... React logs 'Maximum update depth exceeded' after ~50 recursions. Reproduction: log in as demo-delta-supplier, click any sidebar link. Mitigation: change NAV `to` values to absolute paths built from `useParams().sellerSlug`, e.g. `to={`/martbaked/${sellerSlug}/portal/${n.to}`}`. Once fixed, remove or update the inner Route `path='*'` fallback to Navigate to an absolute path as well (`to={`/martbaked/${sellerSlug}/portal/dashboard`}` or a computed react-router `replace` URL) to prevent future recursion.
